## Verified theorem scope

For every fixed kappa>0 and every nonempty negative open interval J_0,
there is a finite complex row in J_0 with M-kappa D_X<0. Consequently L_pi
has a finite negative row on I for kappa=1/(2*pi^2). This is a negative
lower-envelope row only, not a negative V row or an RH result.

## Checks

- The common domain Omega={Re z<0, |Im z|<pi/6} is sufficient: Re a>0 and
  Re(1/a)>1/2. The d_a,j_a endpoint estimates combined with sqrt(r(t)) give
  P_z and Q_z the stated integrable bounds. M and D_X are therefore jointly
  holomorphic on Omega x Omega as unbarred kernels, with conjugation left to
  the external row coefficients.
- The diagonal scaling has the correct Jacobian and powers. Its full-source
  domination bounds M uniformly. The compact U/W rectangle has Q_a bounded
  away from zero and gives D_X>=c_D(-x); all remaining D_X terms are
  nonnegative because the physical cutoff enforces X>=0.
- A1 is applied solely to quadratic K_kappa. It supplies a finite witness in
  each original interval, without treating a distant x as an admissible
  consumer node. The L_pi implication has the correct direction.
- The reciprocity likelihood is exactly j_t=p_(1/t)/p_t=g_(-log t), with
  the t^(-9/2) exponent. The composition and mean identities in (25) are
  correct. j_t is nonconstant for t!=1, so the changed conditional
  projection and potential are correctly retained.
- Under t=1/tau, w(1/t)t^(-2)=w(t), the cutoff becomes [1/H,1], and the
  full transformed signed form (30) and kernel (31) have the correct signs
  and factors. The t=1 trace remains. Covariance cancels only because the
  exact conditional identity is retained; the resulting mean-channel form
  (33) is the unchanged unpaid V sign.

No source pin or mathematical correction is required. The response does not
claim a full positive supplier, a negative V witness, or RH.
